Subject: Post-demo: heartbeat & throttle — load qualification and token-rate asks

Alyssa / Helix infra team — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick written recap so engineering can triage the sizing asks we surfaced. I included Marissa (CS) and Jordan (sales-eng) to help lock down SLOs and next steps.

Recap of what Helix described on the call:
- Primary flow: chunked manifest ingestion + multi-turn enrichment (avg 6 turns) per job
- Mean request size: ~420 tokens (post-tokenization), 95th token size ~2.2x mean
- Expected concurrency: 30 steady concurrent sessions, crest bursts up to ~420 concurrent sessions for short windows (~20s) during nightly batch window
- Streaming behavior: customers watch incremental enrichment; keep long-lived streaming websocket (heartbeat expected every 30s)

Questions / asks (what we need to size Dedicated or recommend Hosted configuration):
1) Confirm p90 latency target for per-token streaming delivery (you mentioned 200–300ms p90). We need a hard target to map to model choice and routing policy.
2) Clarify sustained tokens/sec vs crest tokens/sec across the 20s burst window. You called the crest ~3.6M tokens/s but we need the composition: avg tokens/request during crest, and whether the crest is simultaneous new requests or active continuations.
3) Do streaming sessions hold KV state server-side between messages? If yes, average KV cache size estimate (MB) and expected TTL.
4) Network constraints: are there NAT/GW limits or long TCP connection churn we should know about? The topology PDF you promised will help.

Immediate next steps:
- Helix provides the sample payloads + network diagram (Alyssa) — target 9/8 EOD
- Redwood will run an initial cost/throughput sketch and propose two deployment options (hosted high-priority + small dedicated pool): due 9/9
- Marissa to propose an evaluation SLA and canary plan for the night window pilot

If any of the facts above are off, flag them in a reply and we'll adjust.

Thanks,
Marcus
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — good writeup. Quick answers inline.

- p90 target: 250ms for streaming token flush (internal SLO). We can accept occasional 350ms during night crest but would like carriage under 300ms 95% of the time.
- Crest composition: the 3.6M tokens/s estimate assumes ~420 concurrent new job starts in the first 8s, then many sessions continue for another 12–25s. Avg tokens/request during crest grows to ~520 because we attach enriched metadata.
- KV cache: yes, we retain session KV per open websocket for 300s TTL. Avg per-session KV ~28 KB; worst-case 80 KB.
- Network: we have a VPC NAT gateway with 1200 ephemeral ports available per egress node; we'll attach the topology PDF.

I've attached the sample payloads and the topology PDF to this thread. Hope that helps.

Alyssa
Sr. SRE, HelixCargo

Alyssa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few operational clarifications from CS/ops that will affect the pilot configuration: 

1) Throughput mapping we will use for the pilot (proposed):
   - Steady: 30 concurrent sessions * 420 tokens/request * avg 0.5 requests/sec => ~6.3k tokens/sec sustained
   - Crest window (first 8s): 420 concurrent job starts * 520 tokens/request => ~27.3k tokens/sec sustained during that 8s slice.
   - Ongoing crest continuations raise the 20s-window effective tokens/sec to ~4.1M tokens total (we map to tokens/sec when modeling).

2) Concurrency planning: We'll treat the 420 concurrent starts as an elastic crest and recommend a burst-capable routing policy (mix of dedicated pool + fallback to hosted low-priority) to protect the baseline SLOs.

3) Latency & streaming: To meet the 250ms p90 streaming flush, we recommend:
   - Model choice: a 7B quantized variant with streaming-friendly kernels (lower per-token latency) OR a 13B distilled variant if quality requires it.
   - Autoscaling policy: aggressive fast-start scaling for the first 10s of a crest window, with pre-warmed workers when night window detected via schedule/webhook.
   - Heartbeat handling: Redwood will honor 30s application heartbeats; we'll add keepalive timeouts at 90s on the server side to avoid leaking connections.

4) KV caching: Given 28 KB average and 80 KB worst-case per session, 420 concurrent sessions max -> ~34 MB worst-case. We'll include this in memory planning; caching persists only for active websockets.

Action items and owners: 
- Redwood (Marcus): throughput & cost sketch comparing two deployment options (hosted-priority, small dedicated pool + warmers) — due 2026-09-09 12:00 PDT
- Helix (Alyssa): confirm whether crest starts are scheduled (cron) or event-driven and share any historical crest samples (logs) — due 2026-09-09 EOD
- Redwood-CS (Marissa): draft pilot canary run plan and SLA targets for night window — due 2026-09-10

I'll follow up with a short runbook and a proposed canary schedule once Marcus posts the cost sketch.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
